A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RefTool, with matching authors, core framework, and retained scientific experiments. Their text, tables, figures, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the revised title and expanded scope.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, human tool-quality assessments, computational costs, and additional experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds translation experiments, training-based comparisons, additional tool-creation evaluations, and revised human assessments.

M1.justification: v1 extracts an existing reference hierarchy and generates executable Python tools. v2 adds LLM-generated categories and segment assignment for unstructured references. Its translation adaptation uses pseudo-code tools, model-based verification against parallel examples, and refinement without discarding tools (Sections 2.1, 3.3 and Appendix A.4). These substantially extend the procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains the scientific benchmarks, including the existing SciBench-fund transfer experiment, and adds bidirectional Zhuang–Chinese translation using ZHUANGRULES and 109 grammar rules. This introduces a non-scientific language task and evaluation with initially unstructured reference material, substantially broadening coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds LATM and TroVE, which v1 cited but explicitly excluded from evaluation. v2 also adds continued-pretraining and QA-fine-tuning comparators in Table 8, plus four translation baselines in Table 3: Whole Grammar Book, Retrieval from Whole Book, Rule-by-Rule Retrieval, and its code-augmented variant.

E3.justification: v2 adds BLEU/chrF++ translation evaluation using Llama-3.1-70B and Qwen-2.5-72B, dictionaries, and paired examples. New protocols reserve six test examples for LATM training/validation and use a 10% holdout and two training epochs for training-based comparisons. Human tool-quality sampling increases from 20 to 50 tools per domain; the tool-creation evaluation also adds Llama.

E4.justification: The component ablations, tool-selection consistency study, and case studies are retained. Appendix B.4 extends creator-model robustness from Gemini to include Llama, and Appendix B.6 broadens the existing cost analysis to more comparators. The tool-quality assessment is expanded through larger samples. These extend established analyses without substantially changing their questions.

E5.justification: v2 Section 3.2 newly claims that accuracy aggregated across four LLMs significantly exceeds all baselines in each scientific domain at alpha = 0.05. v1 makes no corresponding significance statement. The addition does not specify the test, exact p-values, confidence intervals, seeds, or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Existing Table 2 rows and Table 4 ablation scores remain unchanged. v2 adds substantial results for new baselines, translation, training alternatives, Llama-created tools, and costs. Translation averages are 54.0 BLEU/61.6 chrF++, versus 43.9/60.0 for code-augmented rule retrieval. Larger-sample human ratings replace earlier estimates, including chemistry faithfulness 90% to 96% and usefulness 95% to 90%; these are not same-sample changes.

T1.justification: The framework notation and Appendix C's selection-consistency formulas remain mathematically equivalent, with chapter renamed category. Reference equations in the example figures are retained. Neither version introduces new theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the central contribution from structured-reference scientific reasoning to unstructured references and non-scientific translation. The abstract's reported average accuracy advantage changes from 11.3% to 12.3% alongside expanded comparisons, while the original benchmark scores remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning translation-rule organization, limitations of direct textbook training, reusable-tool cost amortization, and open-source creation for sensitive references. It removes v1 Appendix E's explicit discussion of general-code/web-agent applicability and foundational-domain requirements. A narrower warning about domain misunderstanding remains in the human-quality discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds category-generation and assignment prompts, translation settings and verification details, and training-data construction and hyperparameters, including two epochs and learning rate 1e-5. The access statement expands from code to code and data. Existing scientific model versions and hardware remain documented, but v1's explicit LaTeX-conversion step and original benchmark question counts are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds translation-related references by Tanzer et al. and Zhang et al., plus the Qwen2.5 report. Section 5 expands the comparison with embedding-based retrieval and distinguishes generated hierarchies from inherited API categories. The existing automatic-tool-creation positioning is largely retained; LATM and TroVE were already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The title and opening/concluding narrative are revised around knowledge-intensive reasoning. Baseline explanations move into Appendix A.3, Section 4 is reordered, and human tool-selection discussion moves to Appendix C. A dedicated generalizability subsection and reorganized implementation appendix are added, while Appendix E changes from limitations to an LLM-use disclosure. Together these substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds translation, training-comparison, and expanded-cost tables; enlarges several comparison tables; and splits v1's human-evaluation Table 3 between main-text Table 6 and appendix Table 14. It adds a knowledge-organization prompt figure, combines selection-prompt figures, relocates the overview figure, and changes the conference layout. Existing case-study graphics retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the framework's applicability: translation tests its extension beyond structured scientific references, while LATM/TroVE and training-based comparisons address important alternatives missing from v1. Open-source tool creation and larger human-quality samples further strengthen validation. Removing explicit limitations and adding an underspecified significance claim weaken transparency, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the substantial gains in testing the method's scope and comparative value.
